messages:
alex: quick question — customer asked for full request/response logs for a debugging run, but they require all PII redacted. do we have an official platform stance on server-side redaction vs leaving it to SDKs? :eyes:

maria: short answer: default to server-side redaction for hosted API. customers can opt into richer logs via enterprise DPA and additional controls. we need clear retention defaults and admin consent flows.

tyler: server-side is safest legally, but engineering concerns: over-redaction can break debugging (eg removing order IDs). proposal: structured whitelist + redaction layers. also need sampling so costs don't blow up.

zoe: UX idea: per-route "Enable request/response logs" toggle + sampling slider (0.1%..100%) + a dropdown: [metadata-only, redacted-text, raw (ent-only)]. show estimated monthly token storage cost in the panel.

sam: technical note — redaction by regex alone will miss a lot of PII and also produce false positives. recommend a small PII classifier (token-level) as first pass, then regex fallback. store classifier score, not matched content.

alex: example log that causes debate:
```json
{
  "request": "Generate email to alice@example.com about order 123-45-6789",
  "response": "Hi Alice, your order 123-45-6789 shipped."
}
```
what do we store for redacted-text? both request and response with emails and numbers redacted? or replace with hashed placeholder?

maria: replace with deterministic salted hash for identifiers where correlation is needed (e.g., user_id), but for emails/SSNs replace with [REDACTED_EMAIL], [REDACTED_SSN]. hashing emails could be considered PII in some jurisdictions, check legal.

tyler: propose three-tier policy by default:
1) metadata-only: no LLM text, just route, model, token counts, salted user hash, latency.
2) redacted-text: server-side PII removal (classifier+regex), keep salted hashes for IDs, retention default 30d.
3) raw logs: only for enterprise with DPA and KMS-wrapped storage, retention per contract.

zoe: console should warn when enabling redacted-text: show what redaction does and a preview example. add an "allowlist" for structured fields (e.g., form.user_id) where customers assert they control data and want raw.

sam: sampling strategy: deterministic hash(user_id, route) -> if hash % 100 < sample_pct then store. fallback reservoir sampler for anonymous traffic. deterministic gives stable replayability for a user.

tyler: edge-case: requests with long contexts and many tokens — recommend storing only last N tokens or a token-sampled tail to limit size. we can also store token count and truncated text.

maria: retention defaults: metadata-only 90d, redacted-text 30d, enterprise configurable up to 365d. all enablement must create an audit entry with admin identity (audit-bot will log).

audit-bot: audit: setting change requested by @alex for route "checkout/assist". will record admin + timestamp when toggle is flipped. :white_check_mark:

alex: implementation plan suggestion:
- tyler: RFC for server-side redaction + sampling algorithm + edge token truncation (week 1)
- sam: prototype PII classifier and eval dataset + metrics for precision/recall (week 1-2)
- zoe: console mock & cost estimator UI + admin consent flow (week 1)
- maria: produce compliance checklist + retention defaults (week 1)
canary targeted for next-month mid-cycle.

tyler: one more debate: should redaction run in the edge layer (closer to customer) or in core service after routing? edge reduces data plane movement but duplicates logic. leaning core service for consistency + single classifier model.

zoe: UX note — show a small badge on the request inspector: "redaction level: metadata-only / redacted / raw" so support can quickly see what's available. also provide a "request replay" button that respects retention and redaction rules.

sam: we'll need a small benchmark: PII classifier latency per request + memory. aim <5ms overhead or run async with best-effort - but async complicates real-time debugging.

alex: sounds like consensus for server-side redaction + deterministic sampling + enterprise raw under DPA. thanks — i'll create the tracking ticket and assign RFC to @tyler.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll add the compliance notes to the ticket.

tyler: I'll start drafting RFC today.

zoe: I'll add UI mocks to the ticket by EOD.

sam: will post initial classifier results in #eng-ml when ready.

alex: :thumbsup:
